newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kremlin official sees stopgap agreement at summit.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin official sees stopgap agreement at summit.

text.p: A senior Russian policy-maker said on Tuesday he believed Boris Yeltsin and Bill Clinton would reach no accord on NATO enlargement at this week's Helsinki summit but could seal an interim deal to continue talks.
Boris Berezovsky, deputy secretary of the policy-making Security Council, told an invited audience in Bonn he was convinced eastward expansion would only create mistrust in Europe.
"I am sure that they will not be able to find a strategic solution, they will probably postpone that," said Berezovsky.
"No one wants a confrontation," he added. "They will find an interim solution which allows them to continue negotiations, but without Russia accepting the principle of NATO enlargement."
Berezovsky has considerable influence in the Kremlin but has not been closely involved in foreign affairs.
NATO wants to issue invitations in July to several eastern European countries to join the alliance, with the front-runners believed to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
At the same time it has offered to formalise Russia's part in shaping Europe's security architecture on terms still to be established.
But Moscow has made clear it sees NATO's planned admission of countries from the former communist Warsaw Pact as damaging to its relations with the West.
Berezovsky said the West must honour Russia's sometimes faltering efforts at democratisation and developing a market economy by giving it a full place in the community of democratic nations.
He said the Russian Revolution earlier this century was an example of what could happen when Russia had not been allowed to play a full part in Europe's common security.
"At a different level, we could return to that period," he said.
"We know we cannot achieve full democracy alone, but you keep telling us: 'go away and try again'."
